newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Bescorp in Indonesian venture.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Bescorp in Indonesian venture.

text.p: Construction and infrastructure firm Bescorp Industries Bhd said on Tuesday it has entered into an agreement with Task Force of Indonesia to jointly privatise waste management in Jakarta.
In a statement, Bescorp said the $2 billion project will be undertaken by a joint-venture company, P.T. Malindo Ciptra Nusantara, which will have an initial paid-up capital of $8 million.

The privatisation will involve the collection and disposal of solid waste, manufacture of recycled raw material for the Indonesian and export markets, and improvement of the sewerage system in the city.
Bescorp will hold a 60 percent equity interest in the joint venture while Task Force and Indonesia's Dinas Kebersihan will hold 20 percent each.
The concession period for the project will be for 50 years.
Bescorp said P.T. Malindo is expected to receive a minimum monthly revenue of $30 million from waste collection in Jakarta.

Bescorp has proposed a rights issue of 20.9 million new shares at 9.70 ringgit per share, proceeds of which will be used as capital requirement for the Indonesian venture, to repay bank borrowings and for working capital.
The company also planned an employees' share option scheme of up to 10 percent of its issued share capital.
Following the proposals, Bescorp's share capital will increase to 45.98 million ringgit from 19.0 million, and net tangible assets per share to 5.61 ringgit from 1.67 ringgit.
Bescorp has requested the lifting of suspension of its shares on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange. The stock was last traded at 23.80 ringgit before the suspension on March 18.
